I farm a small area, 7.5 mu total, and my household only has two people, so I will keep the plan practical and labor-manageable. I have 40 years of experience, so I do not want to gamble on complicated changes. I will put more land into cotton because it fits my usual system better and I know how to manage it steadily, and I will keep a smaller area in stevia for cash income diversification. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on a few planned irrigations instead of waiting on rainfall. I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed because I want stable emergence and more uniform growth, but I will avoid overly aggressive input use because my land area is not large and I care about controlling cost. For cotton, I will use moderate fertilizer with a bit more nitrogen and potassium to support vegetative growth and boll formation, and I will prepare the land with rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale. For stevia, I will use slightly lower nitrogen and balanced phosphorus and potassium because I want steady leaf production rather than excessive soft growth. I will plan several pesticide applications for cotton since insect pressure is usually more important there, and slightly fewer for stevia. My goal is steady yield, manageable labor, and reduced risk rather than pushing for the highest possible output.
